event: UFC Fight Night: Hooker vs. Parnasse

items.fight_news: Dan Hooker headlines UFC Paris as the ranked lightweight name on the card, bringing a 24-14 record and years of UFC experience against elite opposition. The public stakes are clear: he is being asked to defend his top-10 visibility against a newcomer whose reputation was built outside the Octagon.

Salahdine Parnasse enters his UFC debut at 23-2 with a major French spotlight behind him. A main-event debut is an unusually direct test, and a win over Hooker would immediately move him from high-profile signing to live lightweight contender in front of a home-region crowd.

This is a veteran-versus-arrival fight more than a normal rankings matchup. Hooker has the UFC mileage, five-round familiarity, and bigger-name schedule, while Parnasse brings momentum, youth, and the pressure of validating his non-UFC resume on the biggest stage of his career.

The Paris setting matters because Parnasse will likely receive the louder arena reaction, but Hooker has spent much of his UFC run in hostile or high-pressure fights. For users scanning the matchup, the question is whether proven UFC experience can slow a debuting fighter with major local energy.

Fares Ziam gets a prominent lightweight slot on the Paris main card with an 18-5 record and a chance to convert another France appearance into a cleaner step forward. His UFC familiarity gives the bout an established-local angle rather than a pure prospect showcase.

Axel Sola is listed at 12-1-1 and meets Ziam in an all-French lightweight matchup. That makes the fight easy to frame for casual users: two domestic names, one with more UFC exposure and one trying to use the same stage to announce himself.

The co-main placement gives this fight more weight than a standard lightweight booking. Ziam has the broader audience name recognition, but Sola's record keeps the matchup competitive on paper and makes the result meaningful for France's deeper lightweight picture.

bouts.title: Michael Venom Page vs. Nursulton Ruziboev

items.fight_news: Michael Venom Page is listed as the ranked middleweight on the card with a 25-3 record. His name value and unorthodox striking make this one of the easiest main-card fights for casual users to identify, especially with Page still chasing marquee UFC momentum.

Nursulton Ruziboev brings a deep 37-9-2 record and real finishing history into the matchup. He is not just a record-padding opponent; his long professional resume makes him a dangerous test for any striker who gives him clean entries or extended grappling windows.

The public style contrast is distance and movement against physical finishing threat. Page wants space, reads, and highlight counters, while Ruziboev's appeal is that he can make a clean technical fight turn chaotic if he forces exchanges or clinch contact.

Daniil Donchenko is listed at 15-2 by CBS and 14-2 by Sherdog, so his profile should be treated as strong but still fluid during fight week. The important public angle is that he arrives as the fresher welterweight name in a main-card slot.

Punahele Soriano enters at 13-4 with a recognizable UFC profile and experience against tough opposition. Even when his results have been uneven, his physicality and power make him a difficult measuring stick for an opponent trying to establish himself quickly.

This fight is a classic main-card opportunity fight: Donchenko can use a win to prove he belongs in a bigger UFC lane, while Soriano can use the same matchup to remind users that proven UFC rounds still matter against newer arrivals.

Morgan Charriere fights in France with a 21-12-1 record and one of the card's clearer crowd connections. His record has mileage, but that also means he has been through enough different fight types to be more than a simple hometown-action pick.

Felipe Lima enters at 14-2 and gives Brazil one of its key representatives on the Paris card. His cleaner record creates a straightforward contrast with Charriere: the local favorite with experience and support against the visiting fighter with stronger recent profile optics.

The broad public read is pressure and atmosphere against a dangerous, composed underdog spoiler. Charriere's popularity can make momentum feel amplified in the arena, while Lima has the kind of record that keeps this from being a crowd showcase.

Losene Keita is listed at 16-2 and gets a main-card featherweight spot after building a strong European reputation. For public users, the card placement signals that UFC is giving him a real visibility push rather than hiding him in a low-leverage debut lane.

Muhammad Naimov brings a 13-4 record and more UFC name recognition than many opponents used to introduce regional standouts. He gives Keita a credible first major test because he has already operated inside UFC pacing, pressure, and broadcast expectations.

This bout has prospect-evaluation stakes. Keita can turn local-region momentum into immediate featherweight relevance, while Naimov can slow that rise by showing that established UFC experience remains a different standard.

Mario Pinto is listed at 12-0 and opens the televised prelim stretch against a far more familiar name. An undefeated heavyweight with a main-card-adjacent prelim position is exactly the kind of fighter casual users may track as a fast-rising watchlist entry.

Ryan Spann brings a 24-11 record, long UFC experience, and a history of competing at light heavyweight before this heavyweight booking. That makes him the known-risk side of the matchup: inconsistent results, but real finishing danger and veteran poise.

The public hook is unbeaten upside against veteran volatility. Pinto has the cleaner record and fresher trajectory, while Spann's experience means he can still turn one mistake into a fight-changing moment.

Kurtis Campbell enters at 8-1 in a featherweight prelim against a recognizable action fighter. His record and placement suggest a developmental opportunity, but it is not a quiet one because Trevor Peek fights tend to draw attention quickly.

Trevor Peek is listed at 9-3 and is familiar to UFC viewers for his aggressive, physical approach. His style gives the fight an obvious public angle: Campbell may have the cleaner prospect profile, but Peek can make technical plans messy.

Oumar Sy fights in France with a 12-2 record and gets another chance to build momentum in front of a friendly crowd. At light heavyweight, a decisive win can travel quickly because the division often rewards size, finishing threat, and visible athleticism.

Modestas Bukauskas brings a 20-7 record and the deeper UFC resume. He is a useful test for Sy because he has enough experience to punish a younger fighter who relies only on physical advantages or crowd emotion.

The public matchup is local upside against veteran durability. Sy has the cleaner momentum story, while Bukauskas has been around enough high-level situations to make the fight more demanding than a simple showcase.

Nathaniel Wood is listed at 23-6 and appears on multiple current card listings after some official-preview uncertainty around his opponent slot. His UFC familiarity makes this featherweight prelim one of the more notable fights below the main card.

Mairon Santos is listed at 18-1 by CBS and gives Wood a high-record-risk assignment. Even without the biggest mainstream name, Santos' record makes him the type of opponent who can immediately change how users view Wood's divisional standing.

The broad public read is proven UFC experience against a fighter with a much cleaner record. Wood has the recognizable schedule, while Santos brings the statistical profile of someone who should not be treated like a routine prelim opponent.

Michael Aljarouj is listed at 13-3 and gives the Paris prelims another French presence. A flyweight win at home would give him immediate visibility in a division where new names can stand out quickly with pace and clean finishing sequences.

Fabia Sintes enters at 11-3 and brings a similar record range into the matchup. The public-facing angle is a closely matched flyweight fight where neither side is being presented as a record-based showcase opponent.
Nora Cornolle is listed as the ranked women's bantamweight on the card with a 9-4 record. Her France connection and ranking tag give this prelim a clearer stakes line than many lower-card fights.

Klaudia Sygula enters at 8-2 and gets a chance to disrupt a ranked opponent's home-country appearance. For public users, the fight is easy to read as Cornolle defending position while Sygula tries to turn a road assignment into a rankings conversation.

Women's bantamweight can move quickly when ranked names stumble. Cornolle has more visible standing to protect, while Sygula's cleaner record gives her enough credibility to make this more than a stay-busy fight.

bouts.title: Matthieu Duclos vs. Luis Felipe Dias

items.fight_news: Matthieu Duclos fights at home with a 10-3 record in a middleweight prelim. The placement gives French fans another local storyline before the main card, and a win would help separate him from the crowded group of developing European names.

Luis Felipe Dias is listed at 18-5 and gives Brazil a second card representative after Felipe Lima. His higher fight count makes the matchup useful for measuring Duclos against someone who has already handled a longer professional road.

Delphine Benouaich opens the card in France with a 7-2 record and a clear local-interest role. Early prelim placement still matters here because a sharp home performance can make users remember a newer strawweight before the heavier names arrive.

Sofia Montenegro is listed at 6-2 and enters as a similarly experienced opponent on paper. The public angle is a balanced strawweight opener: two developing fighters, close records, and a first chance to set the tone for the Paris card.
